# The Logistic Map {.unnumbered}
<br>

The Logistic Map is given by,
$$
x_{n+1}=rx_n(1-x_n),
$$ {#eq-LogisticEqn}

The behaviour of the population over time looks like,

::: {#fig-logisticapp}

```{shinylive-python}
#| standalone: true
#| components: [viewer]
#| viewerHeight: 500


from shiny import App, Inputs, Outputs, Session, render, ui
from shiny import reactive

import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.integrate import odeint

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.layout_sidebar(
        ui.sidebar(
    ui.input_slider(id="r",label="r",min=0.0,max=5.0,value=1.2,step=0.001),             
    ui.input_slider(id="u0",label="x_0 (Initial condition)",min=0.0,max=1.0,value=0.5,step=0.01),
    ui.input_slider(id="T",label="Number of iterations",min=0.0,max=60.0,value=20.0,step=1.0),
       
        ),

        ui.output_plot("plot"),
    ),
)

def server(input, output, session):
    
    @render.plot
    def plot():
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(1,1)
        
        r=float(input.r())
        u0=float(input.u0())
        T=int(input.T())
        
        def logisticrhs(x,par):
          r=par
          f=r*x*(1.0 - x)
          return f
        # Define rhs of logistic map 
     
        # this function computes the solutio to the difference equation. It also stores solution in format for cobweb plotting
        def SolveSingleDiffAndCobweb(t,rhs,N_0,r):
          # Initialise solution vector
          N = np.zeros_like(t,dtype=float)
          N[0]=N_0


          num_time_steps=t.shape[0]


          # Initialise cobweb solution object
          CobwebSol=np.zeros((2*num_time_steps,2))
          CobwebSol[0,0]=N_0
          CobwebSol[0,1]=rhs(N_0,r)
          CobwebSol[1,0]=CobwebSol[0,1]
          CobwebSol[1,1]=CobwebSol[0,1]

          # loop over time and compute solution.
          for i in t:
            if i>0:
              N[i]=rhs(N[i-1],r) 

              sol_temp=N[i-1]
              rhs_temp=rhs(sol_temp,r)
              CobwebSol[2*i,0]=sol_temp
              CobwebSol[2*i,1]=rhs_temp
              CobwebSol[2*i+1,0]=rhs_temp
              CobwebSol[2*i+1,1]=rhs_temp
          return N, CobwebSol

        # Define discretised t domain
        t = np.arange(0, T, 1)
        # define initial conditions
        init_cond=u0
        
        # Compute numerical solution of ODEs
        y,CobwebSol = SolveSingleDiffAndCobweb(t,logisticrhs,init_cond,r)

        # Plot results
        
        #ax[0].plot(t,y)
        ax.set_ylim(0, 1)
        ax.set_xlim(0, T)
        ax.plot(t, y, linestyle='-', alpha=0.4) # faint line
        ax.plot(t, y, linestyle='None', marker='o',color='C0', ms=3) # solid 
        ax.set_xlabel('$n$')
        ax.set_ylabel('$x_n$')
        ax.set_title('Time series')

        plt.grid()

        plt.show()
    
app = App(app_ui, server)
```

An app to explore the behaviour of the Logistic map.
:::

## Bifurcation diagram
Plot the equilibrum (long time) values for $x_n$ for different values of $r$ to get,

::: {#fig-logisticInteractive}

```{shinylive-python}
#| standalone: true
#| components: [viewer]
#| viewerHeight: 700

import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go

from shiny import App, reactive, ui
from shinywidgets import output_widget, render_widget


# --------------------------------------------------
# Logistic map settings
# --------------------------------------------------

X0 = 0.5

R_SAMPLES = 1800
TRANSIENT = 2000
KEEP = 150

POINT_SIZE = 2
POINT_OPACITY = 0.45


# --------------------------------------------------
# Calculate bifurcation points
# --------------------------------------------------

def calculate_bifurcation(r_min, r_max):

    r_values = np.linspace(r_min, r_max, R_SAMPLES)

    x = np.full(R_SAMPLES, X0)

    # Discard the transient iterations
    for _ in range(TRANSIENT):
        x = r_values * x * (1 - x)

    # Store the long-term behaviour
    points = np.empty((KEEP, R_SAMPLES))

    for i in range(KEEP):
        x = r_values * x * (1 - x)
        points[i, :] = x

    r_points = np.tile(r_values, KEEP)
    x_points = points.ravel()

    return r_points, x_points


# --------------------------------------------------
# Shiny user interface
# --------------------------------------------------

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(

    ui.h2("Logistic Map: Bifurcation Diagram"),

    ui.p(
        "Drag a rectangle over the diagram to zoom into "
        "a region."
    ),

    ui.input_action_button(
        "reset",
        "Reset diagram"
    ),

    ui.hr(),

    output_widget("bifurcation"),

    ui.p(
        "Horizontal axis: r",
        " | ",
        "Vertical axis: N"
    )
)


# --------------------------------------------------
# Shiny server
# --------------------------------------------------

def server(input, output, session):

    # Current viewing limits
    view = reactive.value((0.0, 4.0, 0.0, 1.0))


    # Reset the diagram
    @reactive.effect
    @reactive.event(input.reset)
    def reset_view():

        view.set((0.0, 4.0, 0.0, 1.0))


    # Handle rectangular selections
    def on_select(trace, points, state):

        if len(points.xs) == 0:
            return

        selected_r = np.asarray(points.xs, dtype=float)
        selected_n = np.asarray(points.ys, dtype=float)

        r0 = float(np.min(selected_r))
        r1 = float(np.max(selected_r))

        n0 = float(np.min(selected_n))
        n1 = float(np.max(selected_n))

        # Add a little padding around the selected points
        r_padding = max((r1 - r0) * 0.05, 0.005)
        n_padding = max((n1 - n0) * 0.08, 0.005)

        r0 = max(0.0, r0 - r_padding)
        r1 = min(4.0, r1 + r_padding)

        n0 = max(0.0, n0 - n_padding)
        n1 = min(1.0, n1 + n_padding)

        # Avoid zero-width or zero-height views
        if r1 <= r0 or n1 <= n0:
            return

        view.set((r0, r1, n0, n1))


    # Draw the interactive diagram
    @render_widget
    def bifurcation():

        r_min, r_max, n_min, n_max = view.get()

        # Recalculate the points for the current r range
        r_points, n_points = calculate_bifurcation(
            r_min,
            r_max
        )

        # Create an interactive Plotly figure
        fig = go.FigureWidget(

            data=[
                go.Scattergl(
                    x=r_points,
                    y=n_points,
                    mode="markers",
                    marker=dict(
                        size=POINT_SIZE,
                        opacity=POINT_OPACITY
                    ),
                    hoverinfo="skip",
                    showlegend=False
                )
            ]
        )

        # Listen for rectangular selections
        fig.data[0].on_selection(on_select)

        fig.update_layout(

            title="Logistic Map Bifurcation Diagram",

            xaxis=dict(
                title="r",
                range=[r_min, r_max],
                autorange=False
            ),

            yaxis=dict(
                title="x_e",
                range=[n_min, n_max],
                autorange=False
            ),

            dragmode="select",

            selectdirection="any",

            height=600,

            margin=dict(
                l=65,
                r=30,
                t=65,
                b=60
            ),

            template="plotly_white",

            uirevision="constant"
        )

        return fig


app = App(app_ui, server)
```

An app to explore the behaviour of the Logistic map.
:::
